maps.title: Harinama Cintamani · Session 09 · Offence #4 - Criticising the Scriptures

nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj explains the fourth offence, criticising scripture. With four defects we are like someone who cannot see without glasses, and the surest way to punish a conditioned soul is to take scripture away; the Vedas are the universe's manual and our mother. He outlines the nine teachings of the Vedas, the six philosophers who rejected their purport, and the remedy of honouring the Bhagavatam. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Haridasa Thakura names the fourth offence, criticism of the scriptures, which also obstructs one's chanting.

🎙 Maharaj at 05:50 (auto-transcript): “A fourth offence is criticism of scripture. This offence will also obstruct once. This approach is not so nice this time.”

The four Vedas, the Upanishads and the Puranas emanated from Krishna's breathing, so they are perfect knowledge and the final proof, above all in spiritual matters.

🎙 Maharaj at 07:05 (auto-transcript): “Scripture means the four Vedas, the Upanishads, and the Puranas. Shastra ka matlab hai, chaar Ved, Puran, or Upanishad. Ine shastra bolte hai. Having emanated from the breathing of Krishna, the sastra constituted perfect knowledge and authority. Ye sabhi Bhagavan Shri Krishna…”

Scriptures are not mundane novels. Every machine comes with a manual; the universe, Krishna's product, has one too, showing where we belong and what our duty is. — “the universe which is the product of krishna also has a manual”

🎙 Maharaj at 08:15 (auto-transcript): “The sastras, they are not like mundane novels. just like every material product we have has a manual how to operate the machine the universe which is the product of krishna also has a manual which are the scriptures”

Every human being has four defects, so without the light of revealed description we are effectively blind.

🎙 Maharaj at 09:32 (auto-transcript): “In human life, we have four defects. Therefore, we are considered blind. To have the light, we need description. We are faced with four defects.”

Our perception is limited: even with eyeglasses we don't see, hear or act perfectly. How then can we transcend duality and reach perfection on our own? — “We need the scriptures to take us out of our illusions.”

🎙 Maharaj at 10:42 (auto-transcript): “We have limited perception. In perfect senses, in perfect senses, our senses are not perfect, even with our eyeglass. We don't see perfectly. We don't hear perfectly.”
When Krishna left this world, the Srimad-Bhagavatam rose like the sun of the Puranas for those who have lost their sight in the darkness of Kali-yuga.

The other defects: being in illusion, the tendency to cheat, and inattention of the senses. Senses cannot reach beyond matter, so Krishna gave the Vedas, which are free of these defects.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:33 (auto-transcript): “Second purpose is Brahma, not Brahma, Brahma, I mean this illusion. Vipralipsa, Desire to report something other than what is preceded. And Pramada, inattention of the senses, inattention of the senses.”

children.topic: How to punish a conditioned soul
children.note:
Maharaj asks: if you want to punish someone who cannot see without glasses, what do you do? And how would you punish a soul with four defects?

🎙 Maharaj at 15:24 (auto-transcript): “If you want to punish a person who cannot say without their glass, what do you do? What to do?”

The answer from the audience: take away his glasses. Likewise, the way to punish a conditioned soul is to remove scripture from his life — he says he is testing their hearing. — “Take away the glass.”

🎙 Maharaj at 15:24 (auto-transcript): “If you want to punish a person who cannot say without their glass, what do you do? What to do?”

Remove the Bhagavatam, the Gita and the Caitanya-caritamrta from ISKCON and what is left? The audience answers: a disaster, aimless, substanceless — a society for maya consciousness. — “Society for Maya Consciousness.”

🎙 Maharaj at 18:28 (auto-transcript): “So if you remove Bhagwatam, Chita Chita, Chita, Chita, Rita from ISKCON, what would ISKCON be? Remove Bhagwatam, remove Bhagwatam, take away Chita. Net of devotion to ISKCON. How would you call ISKCON? Indian tradition. Huh? If you remove Bhagwatam and Bhagwatam from ISKCON,…”
Krishna is very clear in the Gita: one who discards scriptural injunction and acts whimsically attains neither perfection, happiness nor the supreme goal. No scripture means no Godhead, no life.

What is a baby's life without its mother? Helpless, without shelter, full of suffering. That is our life without the Vedas; we need scripture as a baby needs its mother.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:38 (auto-transcript): “because another example another example I will give is what did they use for their child without the mother? So the life of a baby without the mother helpless completely helpless he will become man-less yes”

And when a child criticises and blasphemes its mother, how will it live? It suffers. Maharaj mentions Kamsa and his mother Padmavati: such a person's shelter is taken away and he is never happy.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:33 (auto-transcript): “So when a child starts to criticize blood-fame and crucify the mother, how will they lie? Suffer. Kamsa's mother, Kamsa's mother, Kamsa, Kamsa's mother, he was not good, no mess, Kamsa's”

Minimising, burning or tearing scripture — for any reason, even in the name of religion — brings reactions we cannot handle.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:11 (auto-transcript): “So criticizing the scripture or minimizing the scripture or sometimes I've seen someone burning the scripture or dearing the scripture. You can do that in the name of religion. whatever whatever may be the reason the reason for doing that whatever may be the reason for doing…”

Even a Vaishnava who disrespects the Quran, the Bible or the Torah faces consequences, because they too teach something about God.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:40 (auto-transcript): “Even if a Vaishnava, even if a Vaishnava disreferts Quran, Bible, Torah, its consequences because they are teaching something about God. That verse from Bhagavad Gita 1623, Lord Krishna used the word”

The Gita's word for acting outside scripture is whimsical action under the pull of desire. Such activity, conducted under ignorance, cannot be offered to Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:06 (auto-transcript): “That verse from Bhagavad Gita 1623, Lord Krishna used the word and proper translated acting whimsically in lust. Wimsical activity is dangerous.”

Anyone can say only my religion and my scripture are bona fide and yours are useless. Saying it does not change reality. — “But it does not change the reality.”

🎙 Maharaj at 29:38 (auto-transcript): “One may say, because only my religion is bona fide and my scripture is bona fide. Your scripture is a religion useless. I can say that. I can say that. Anyone can say that. But it does not change the reality. The wise man will understand that karma and gyan are secondary,…”

A wise person sees karma and jnana as secondary and bhakti as the essence. The Vedas teach nine topics, grouped as sambandha (our relationship with Krishna), abhidheya (activity in that relationship) and prayojana (the result, prema).

🎙 Maharaj at 30:44 (auto-transcript): “The Vedas has nine topics, nine subjects. Vedas stand as the authoritative guide and reference Brahmaana and they prove nine different which may be classified into”

There is one Supreme Lord Vishnu, possessor of all energies — not mere light. Even light, Maharaj shows the class, has brightness, heat, colour and a form occupying space. — “Light has qualities.”

🎙 Maharaj at 35:00 (auto-transcript): “Summary of that is, one, there is one Supreme Lord Vishnu, one. The Lord is a possessor of all energies. The Lord is not alone.”

Krishna is the fountainhead of all rasa, Rasaraja, giving joy to the jivas eternally in his abode. His abode, form, name and pastimes are all eternal.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:00 (auto-transcript): “Thirdly, Krishna is the fountainhead of all Rasa, and He is situated in His Dhan, where He eternally gives joy to the Jeevas. So sweet. Krishna is”

Quizzing the class on the Gita's 'millennium after millennium', Maharaj explains that even Krishna's creating and destroying is an eternal activity; the material world is temporary, not false. — “they are temporal but not false”

🎙 Maharaj at 40:46 (auto-transcript): “Bhagavad Gita says, What does that mean? What is the meaning of that? What is the meaning of that? What is the meaning? This is your scripture. I'm asking you from your scripture. From after millennium, after millennium. Good. Millennium after millennium. So what does it mean…”

Jivas are particles of the Lord, unlimited in number, tiny but conscious. Some are bound since time immemorial, attracted to pleasure, yet the Supreme Father punishes no one forever. — “There is a chance for us to get delivered.”

🎙 Maharaj at 43:39 (auto-transcript): “5. Some jivas are eternally bound in the material universes, being attracted by lucrative pleasure. Eternally Bound means that we have been existing here like eternity.”

children.topic: One energy, one with and different
children.note:
Some jivas are eternally liberated in Krishna's service. Krishna exists with his material, jiva and spiritual energies, simultaneously one with and different from them, by inconceivable power.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:21 (auto-transcript): “Seven, Krishna exists with his energies, the material energy, jiva energy and spiritual energy in a state of simultaneous identity and difference permeating all, yet remaining aloof which is only possible by his inconceivable power a chinted bit of that”

Six philosophers in India's history invented theories against the Vedas' real purport and came to no good end; a wise person rejects them, since following them leaves no place for real bhakti.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:47 (auto-transcript): “In the history of India, there are six personalities who invented theories and by their inventions he simply brought themselves to no good end. No good end. All of them no good end.”

Jaimini claims to follow the Vedas but does not recognise the Supreme Lord and stresses fruitive ritual as independent worship.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:52 (auto-transcript): “There are six philosophers. One, Jaymini, though claiming to follow the Vedas does not recognize the Supreme Lord, I recommend Karma Khand activity in independent worship of God. Jaymini ji says that the Karma Khand is the most stressed. But that is Yes, Srila Gurudev, I do.…”

The atheistic Kapila who concluded there is no Lord and taught yoga without its goal is a different person from Kapila, son of Devahuti. — “It's a different Kapil, not equivalent to the son of Devahuti.”

🎙 Maharaj at 50:38 (auto-transcript): “Next, Kapil, by concoction, Kapil thinks that the Lord is imperfect. I recommend the process of yoga without understanding its goal. Kapil is anuman par pohunchta hai ki param bhagawan ka asthita hi nahi hai. Not Kapil, the son of Devahuti, not that. It's a different Kapil,…”

The Jains preached against the Vedas, Carvaka Muni had no respect for Vedic knowledge, and Gautama Buddha did not worship the Lord.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:27 (auto-transcript): “Taking short of the philosophy that everything is illusion, The Jain preached against the Vedas. The 80s Charabaka Muni had no respect for the Vedic knowledge. And similarly, the Buddhist Gautam does not worship the Lord but instead thinks in terms of human beings. In the…”

Vyasadeva is the greatest philosopher, but he is not among them because he accepts the Supreme Person. Chanting the name while holding these philosophies is a serious offence.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:04 (auto-transcript): “In the least, Biasadev is not mentioned here, although he is the greatest philosopher, but his name is not yet. because his teaching is accepting the supreme person with a small bag of water.”

children.topic: Criticising the Vedas, criticising the name
children.note:
The Vedas teach chanting of the pure name as the principal process, so criticising them criticises the name. Devotees take shelter of the Vedas and taste the nectar of the name; even in the spiritual sky great souls chant it.

🎙 Maharaj at 54:36 (auto-transcript): “The purpose is this, since the Vedas are teaching chanting of the pure name as a principal process, to criticize the Vedas is to criticize the name. That is offensive. The devotees, however, take shelter of the Vedas, and by chanting the holy name, attain the nectar of the…”

With attention, one should offer flowers and tulasi leaves to the Bhagavatam and the Vedas. living the…”

We study these details to give up all offences. By the mercy of the name, of pure devotees and of Krishna, if we stick to the process we will be free and go back home, never to see these things again. — “eventually we're going to be free.”

🎙 Maharaj at 63:47 (auto-transcript): “That's why we are studying all these details so that we'll be able to give up all offenses, and by the mercy of the Holy Name, the mercy of pure devotees, the mercy of Krishna. nodeData.topic: Session 10 · Offence #5 - Interpreting the Holy Name
nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj explains the fifth offence: treating the glories of the holy name as exaggeration or interpreting them away. After a long reading of the name's glories, he tells of visiting a group devoted to the Vishnu-sahasra-nama and asking whether their envy and anger were decreasing, and stresses that the Lord has invested all his energies in his name, so we should chant rather than argue. Questions turn to the restless mind, the voices of the three modes and steady practice. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

🎙 Maharaj at 06:34 (auto-transcript): “The fifth offense is giving interpretation to the name and it's glorious. The similarities or Puranas glorify the holy name of Krishna, stating that if one should change the name either in negligence or in faith, Krishna would show that person great There is no knowledge as…”

🎙 Maharaj at 07:17 (auto-transcript): “There is no knowledge as pure as the honey name. There is no vow as powerful as the holy name.”

maps.title: Harinama Cintamani · Session 11 · Offence #6 - Committing Sins

nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj takes up the sixth offence: committing sin on the strength of the holy name. Chanting is meant to give love of Krishna, not to cancel planned sins; the devotee on the road between a sinful and a pure life must add no new sins, and finds safety in the association of pure Vaishnavas. Questions cover how to recognise progress and a pure devotee, why old sinful tastes persist, setting right a wrong report, and complacency after years in bhakti. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:

Maharaj explains in English and Hindi that Pariksit Maharaja did not think, now I have the answer, I can go back to my kingdom. He listened with full attention until the moment of departure, and departed successfully.

children.topic: The name gives prema, not just erasure
children.note:
Chanting is not merely a counter-measure against our sins; its purpose is to give love of Krishna. Atonement rituals can neutralise a sin but cannot redeem the soul, which is why bhakti was praised over prayascitta. — “The chanting of the holy name is not just to counteract our sinful activities.”

🎙 Maharaj at 07:04 (auto-transcript): “The chanting of the holy name is not just to counteract our sinful activities. It is to give us Krishna Prem. In the scriptures we show that all prajastita processes are meant for contracting sins but not to redeem the soul.”

Maharaj recalls that the scriptures reject atonement rituals as the final answer, since they leave the root untouched; bhakti alone is presented as the real cure.

🎙 Maharaj at 07:21 (auto-transcript): “In the scriptures we show that all prajastita processes are meant for contracting sins but not to redeem the soul. So, an intelligent disciple of Parishit Maharaj condemned the process of Prayasthita and he appreciated Bhakti as the solution.”

nodeData.topic: Session 13 · Offence #8 - Equating Holy Name with Rituals
nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. The eighth offence is to put the holy name on the level of Vedic pious rituals and atonements. Maharaj contrasts atonement, which only cuts the grass or patches the tube, with the name, which uproots sin and is always fresh; he tells the story of the monkeys' Ekadasi to show the danger of faithlessness, and explains that the name comes from Goloka and is both the means and the goal. In the questions he speaks on why a guru is compulsory, atoning by confession, chanting loudly while healthy, and humility. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

maps.title: Harinama Cintamani · Session 14 · Offence #9 - Inattentiveness

nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Opening chapter 12, Maharaj explains the ninth offence, inattentive chanting, which can block love of God even when the other offences are avoided. He takes its three forms — indifference, laziness and distraction — with their remedies: holy places, Tulasi, the association of devotees with a taste for the name, quiet focused chanting, and constant prayer for help. Questions cover past-life desires, work worries during japa, chanting in the office, chanting while walking, and chanting with a recording. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
A new chapter: Haridasa Thakura tells Sanatana Gosvami in Puri that inattentive chanting is a great offence.

🎙 Maharaj at 05:11 (auto-transcript): “Inattentiveness Enchanting Holy Name is a great offense. Asaudhani Purwak naam jab karna ek mahan apraad hai. Aaj ka yadhai bara suruh ho raha hai. Harada Sakura spoke to Sanatana Goswami in Puri.”

One may overcome every other offence and chant continuously, yet love of God does not come; the reason is pramada, inattention.

🎙 Maharaj at 07:01 (auto-transcript): “Even if one successfully overcomes all the other offenses in chanting, and one is chanting continuously, the love of God may not come. One should know that the reason for that is that one is committing the offense, known as Brahman or inattention. If someone could do all the…”
In the Bhagavatam pramada is used for madness, as in Rishabhadeva's teaching to his sons; here it means inattention and carelessness.

On the expressway there is always a sign warning against careless driving. Careless japa is the same — and from this offence all the others spring. — “Careless driving is dangerous.”

🎙 Maharaj at 10:05 (auto-transcript): “On the expressway, an express road, there's always a sign. Careless driving is dangerous. Similarly, careless japa. It is from this offense that all other offenses bring.”

The wise recognise three: indifference, laziness and distraction.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:08 (auto-transcript): “The wise men recognize three types of inattention. One is indifference. Indifference or no attention. The second is laziness. And the third one is distraction.”

Something else seems more important — chanting while discussing other subjects, or answering a phone call. That is pramada.

🎙 Maharaj at 12:05 (auto-transcript): “Distraction means that some other things are more important that is taking our attention away from Jap. Just like one is chanting and having discussion. We are not discussing about the name. We are discussing about some other objects. or we are answering a phone call.”

Attached to material things, one chants while the heart is absorbed in some object; chanting all day this way brings no benefit, because not one drop of taste has entered the heart.

Though chanting Japa Delhi, if his taste is so weird, he will show indifference to the name. His heart will not be absorbed in chanting the name, but in some…”

Maharaj counts them with the audience: chant where Krishna had his pastimes — Vrindavan, Puri, Mayapur; near Tulasi Devi; in the company of Vaishnavas; and gradually increase the quality and quantity.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:57 (auto-transcript): “How many items? Remedy? How many items? How many items? One is what? Chants in the places where Krishna performed, Paisan, Vrindavan, Haridva, Jagannathpuri, Maya Purudham, etc. Two chants near Tulsi Devi. And look at Tulsi A.B.”

nodeData.topic: Session 15 · Offence #10 - Considering I and Mine
nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. The tenth and lowest offence is attachment to 'I and mine', the exact opposite of surrender. Maharaj goes through the six qualities of surrender with sharp examples — the devotee who throws out spouse and job, amulets for the stars, the servant whose only word is yes, Krishna as the supreme sanctioning officer — and shows that freedom comes through association, repentance and constant chanting. In the questions he explains how office work becomes service, loyalty in family rituals, serious chanting, honest Ekadasi, and accepting the unfavourable favourably, with SB 10.14.8. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

maps.title: Harinama Cintamani · Session 16 · Offences to the Deities

nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Haridasa Thakura begins the second-last chapter, on offences in serving the deity, after showing that one should not refuse a service the Lord requests. Maharaj walks through the list with practical illustrations: barefoot feet that carry dirt, Uddhava bowing to the dust of the gopis' feet, never-dry prayer, the same Lord at every hour, and the best articles for Krishna. Questions cover food at relatives' homes, home deities, living near the temple and the value of every service. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Mahaprabhu asks Haridasa Thakura to describe the offences in serving the deity. Haridasa first says the deity servants know this better, then agrees to speak. Maharaj draws the lesson: one should not be so humble that one refuses a service the Lord himself is requesting.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:38 (auto-transcript): “That means that one should not be too humble not to do service when the Lord is requesting. You saw the same thing with Kalab Maharaj. Allah Maharaj, pray to Allah Nusimha there. First of all, I love Brahma.”

Maharaj recalls Prahlada Maharaja before Lord Nrsimhadeva: Brahma and the great sages know how to glorify you, what can a boy from a demon family say? Yet he prays because he is asked, and his simple heartfelt prayer pleases the Lord more than ornate praise.

Not scholarship, opulence or fame but devotion is what controls the Lord. When the servant speaks on request, it is really the Lord speaking through him. — “This is the devotion that the Lord is controlled by.”

🎙 Maharaj at 13:26 (auto-transcript): “So, it is not the squirture, it is not the opulence, it is not the fame, This is the devotion that the Lord is controlled by. So Haridasa Kura says, I will elaborate because you're asking me. That means that it's the Lord speaking and the servant is simply the medium, the…”

Many offences against the deity are listed in scripture, in one place 32 and elsewhere 50. Haridasa groups them into four: offences in directly serving the deity, in establishing a deity, in taking darshan, and general offences.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:36 (auto-transcript): “Concerning service to the Murti of the Lord, there are many offences listed in the scriptures. He won't place 32 offences unmentioned and elsewhere 50. And then I have divided these offenses into four types.”

The first offence is entering the temple with shoes on. Maharaj puts a question to the audience: if one walks to the temple barefoot, is that wearing shoes into the temple or not?

🎙 Maharaj at 17:15 (auto-transcript): “So I want to ask a question. 1. Should not walk into the temple with the shoes. So, my question is, if one walks with bare feet, no shoes, and you walk to the temple like that, is it wearing shoes to the temple or not wearing shoes?”

Most devotees reply that walking in with unwashed bare feet is the same as wearing shoes, since the dirt of the road is carried inside.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:48 (auto-transcript): “So, the majority of devotees mention that if one is walking with their feet and walking to the temple is the same as wearing shoes to the temple. Many devotees agree to that. So, this was the question of Guruji, and many people have given me that if there is no temple outside…”

One devotee answers that we should wash our feet before entering; Maharaj accepts this as correct, and says most of us who do not wash are in effect wearing shoes into the temple.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:06 (auto-transcript): “Vishwam brother Prabhu asked Aksa the question. He said we should wash our feet before entering the temple. temple. That means Krishna was washing his feet before he entered the temple. So Krishna is correct. Most of us who are not washing feet before entering, we are wearing…”
Krishna sent Uddhava from Dvaraka to Vrindavan. Overwhelmed by the gopis' devotion, Uddhava offered his prayers not to the gopis themselves but to the dust of their feet.

It was the gopis, not the cowherd boys, whose foot-dust Uddhava honoured. Their love cannot be equalled, and Mahaprabhu confirms there is no better way to worship Krishna than the way they established.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:19 (auto-transcript): “That means what? The Gopis' love is supreme. It cannot be equal. Confirmed by Lord Jitam Mahaprabhu. that there is no better way to serve Christa than depart established by the Gopis. Okay, let's continue. Number two, entering on the palanquin.”

Devotees often complain that their prayers feel dry and repetitive. Maharaj answers with Uddhava, who prayed again and again in ecstasy: prayer itself is never dry, our prayers are dry because there is no feeling in them. — “So prayer is never dry”

🎙 Maharaj at 22:49 (auto-transcript): “Most of us, many devotees have told me many times, when I pray, sometimes it becomes so dry because I will repeat the same thing. It becomes very dry. What to do? Thank you very much.”

The dust of a pure devotee's feet, the feet themselves and the water that washes them all nourish pure bhakti. So a pure devotee may walk anywhere barefoot and purify the place, while those not on that level should wash their feet before entering.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:06 (auto-transcript): “That means what? We have already discussed that the doors from the feet of a pure Bhakti, the foot of them and the water that washes their feet, these three things are conducive for pure Bhakti. so whatever they do from the supreme president”

Further offences: arriving in a palanquin, neglecting festivals, and not offering obeisances.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:02 (auto-transcript): “Number two, entering on the palanquin. That means false ego. The only king is Krishna. Every one of us is Saravan. So walking with the palanquin means we are trying to compete with Krishna. So, it is not correct.”

Entering on a palanquin is false ego. Krishna is the only king and all of us are servants; riding in is an attempt to compete with him. — “The only king is Krishna.”

🎙 Maharaj at 29:09 (auto-transcript): “That means false ego. The only king is Krishna. Every one of us is Saravan. So walking with the palanquin means we are trying to compete with Krishna. So, it is not correct. Number three, not observing festivals.”

All festivals should be fully observed, beginning with the fast, and devotees should always take part.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:52 (auto-transcript): “Number three, not observing festivals. All festivals should be fully celebrated, means we should do the first thing first, the first thing is fasting, we should do that, we should do that, we should do that first.”

Devotees bow to the deity during the program but walk past without obeisances at other times. Maharaj asks: is he not the Lord when there is no program? He is the same person at every hour. — “He is the same Lord”

🎙 Maharaj at 31:24 (auto-transcript): “Number four, not paying obeisances. When we have a program, devotee comes to temple over obeisances, but during the day, when there is no program, devotee will walk past the dating without obeisances. He is not the Lord”

🎙 Maharaj at 45:51 (auto-transcript): “Offering flowers without a fragrance. Offering incense without a fragrant flower. Offering a suitable flower during puja means flowers that have no aroma. Bina kisi sugandh ke pushp arpit nahin karne chahiye.”

children.topic: Avoid both seva and nama offences
children.note:
These offences obstruct bhakti, so anyone who worships the deity should avoid offences both in service and to the holy name.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:30 (auto-transcript): “All these offenses in serving the deity will obstruct one's bhakti. Anyone worshipping the deity should avoid these offences. A devotee should avoid both seva and naama parades.”

When a devotee commits an offence in service he should rectify it immediately; with offences to the name the work of correcting, improving and avoiding goes on constantly.

One on the level of bhava worships the deity day and night in solitude, in his mind, and so commits no offences either in service or to the name.

🎙 Maharaj at 54:55 (auto-transcript): “One who is on the level of bhava worship the deity day and night in solitude. He makes no offences against the name or in service because his service is performed in his mind. On the order of Haridash Thakura, the devotees change the stone of the Gulli name.”

The great preacher returns from converting the world to a temple with no prasadam, a dirty floor and neglected deities. We need pujaris, cleaners, cooks and preachers alike; no one can claim to be best.

maps.title: Harinama Cintamani · Session 17 · The Method of Bhajana (Part 1)

nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Opening the final chapter, Maharaj shows that rasa is the pure nature of the Absolute, not worldly emotion, and that it needs the spiritual world as its setting. With playful analogies (a director turned doorman, a boxer's shame) he explains why the tiny soul is mercifully covered by illusion. The name then blossoms like a flower, revealing Krishna's form, qualities and pastimes right here, and rasa is cooked from its ingredients by the descent of Bhakti-devi. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: How does one qualify for rasa?
children.note:
In the final chapter, on the method of bhajana, Mahaprabhu asks Haridasa Thakura to explain the rasa in the holy name and how the jiva becomes qualified for it. Maharaj asks whether it comes by forming a club or by jumping straight to the Tenth Canto.

🎙 Maharaj at 08:29 (auto-transcript): “How does the Jeeva get qualification to the Rasa in the name? Is it by forming a club? Is it by jumping from to one to nine and to ten? Is that the process?”

Some abandon the Gita as mere fighting and jump to the Tenth Canto's fifth chapters. Haridasa will instead give the real key for entering bhakti-rasa, not secret shortcuts.

Rasa is the highest, purest state of the Absolute, not the sentiments of this world.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:17 (auto-transcript): “This Rasa is not the emotions or sentiment in the material world. But it is the inherent nature of the Absolute Pure.”

What passes for romance in films is a perverted reflection of real rasa. Iron and gold, heaven and hell, cannot be compared. — “There is no comparison.”

🎙 Maharaj at 12:17 (auto-transcript): “Perverted reflection is a Bollywood. That's a perverted demonic reflection of Dr. Lars. There is no comparison. Iron and gold cannot be compared. Heaven and hell cannot be compared. They are completely opposite. It is undimited, full of bliss.”

maps.title: Harinama Cintamani · Session 18 · The Method of Bhajana (Part 2)

nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Completing Harinama-cintamani, Maharaj likens rasa to a meal: our struggles in chanting are the ingredients, and tasting is the perfection beyond dharma, artha, kama and moksa. Faith is given by the sadhu, the guru gives Krishna in the mantra, loud kirtan is more powerful than silent remembrance, and we should chant convinced that Radha and Krishna stand before us. Haridasa outlines the eleven items and five stages of perfection, and in the questions Maharaj urges planning one's Krishna consciousness and compassion for others. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
After the ingredients of rasa are combined, initial love turns into full rasa, the highest perfection. Maharaj compares it to cooking: gather the ingredients, cook, offer to Krishna, and then comes the enjoyment of what you have prepared.

🎙 Maharaj at 08:00 (auto-transcript): “When one starts to cook, when one starts cooking, you get all the ingredients and then you start cooking all the different ingredients. when you put all together you finish cooking what everything is finished and offer to Krishna what is the next thing? Enjoyment, relation…”

The Vedas give four human goals: dharma, artha, kama and moksa. They are meant to lead to the supreme goal, rasa; as there is no meal without cooking, there is no liberation without the earlier steps.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:56 (auto-transcript): “For a person who is not cooking, they have no enjoyment. So, if our vegetables are in the bhojan, if they are not good enough, then we will not be able to eat in prasad.
